name: @projexlight/service-semantic
summary: Backing service for sdk-semantic (G9 closer) — runs the ontology / intent / policy engine as a long-lived process so resolveIntent stays sub-second under load. Hosts the policy evaluator + ontology cache + cross-domain bridge registry. Composes with sdk-ai-gateway for the LLM round-trip behind intent resolution.

events.name: semantic-service.intent.resolved.v1
events.description: Intent resolved end-to-end; carries plan + policy decisions + cost.

events.name: semantic-service.policy.warned.v1
events.description: Policy fired a reshape; downstream UI shows the warning.

hooks.name: startService
hooks.description: Boot service; warm ontology cache; subscribe to relevant events.

hooks.name: resolveIntent
hooks.description: Translate plain-English intent → plan + policy decisions.

hooks.name: registerCapability
hooks.description: Wire an MCP capability into the cross-domain graph (FR-SEM-9).

hooks.name: warmOntology
hooks.description: Pre-load ontology versions for fast resolveIntent on first call.

scenarios.title: Boot warms the ontology cache
scenarios.when_to_use: Process startup — load every active ontology version into Redis-backed cache so first request resolves in tens of ms.
scenarios.example_code:
import { startService } from '@projexlight/service-semantic';
await startService({ warm_ontologies: true });

scenarios.title: Resolve plain-English intent → plan + policy decisions
scenarios.when_to_use: Cloud-builder agent calls resolveIntent; service evaluates against cached ontology + policy + emits the resolution event.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Plan + decisions returned in <500ms. Emits .intent.resolved.v1 with cost attribution.

scenarios.title: Strict-mode policy reshapes a too-broad query
scenarios.when_to_use: PII-sensitive intent; policy reshapes; emit .policy.warned.v1 so the caller UI shows the reshape banner.
scenarios.example_code: // inside resolveIntent: when reshape applies, emit warned event
scenarios.expected_outcome: Caller gets the reshaped plan + UI shows the warning. Audit chain pins the policy decision.

scenarios.title: Register an MCP tool into the cross-domain graph
scenarios.when_to_use: sdk-mcp-bridge installs a new MCP server; the service registers each tool into the capability graph so cross-domain intents can route to it.
scenarios.example_code:
import { registerCapability } from '@projexlight/service-semantic';
await registerCapability({ tenant_id, mcp_server, tool_name, capability_kind, bridges_to });
scenarios.expected_outcome: Capability registered + .capability.registered.v1 emitted. Future intents resolve through the new tool.

scenarios.title: Reactive: new ontology version → cache reload
scenarios.when_to_use: Reactive on semantic.ontology.published.v1 — service loads the new version into cache so subsequent resolveIntent calls use it.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Cache updated within seconds. Old ontology version retained for resolveIntent calls that pinned to it.

compliance_posture.notes: Every intent resolution carries the ontology version + matched policy rules — fully reproducible for EU AI Act decision-trace + GDPR Art-22 automated-decision audits. Cache invalidation strict so a published ontology change takes effect within seconds.
